g.text: Findings · a round on your own pull request
3 reviews on 2 pull requests waiting for a decision
3 findings. Give each one a verdict and a comment if you have one; Save comments keeps them here and on the pull request, and Complete appears once every finding is
HIGH Unbounded query loads every session into memory
The loop would have parked it: needs a migration review.
Use a composite index with project_id
A note for the pull request and the fix session (optional)
Findings · a review of somebody else's pull request
2 findings, already on the pull request. Read them there; Reply says something on a finding’s own thread, Delete takes one out of the review itself, and Complete
takes this card off the queue and leaves the rest to the pull request’s author.
CRIT Token written to the log in plain text
LOW Typo in the settings label
No review is waiting. Findings arrive here from ⌕ Code review and from every review-loop round.
Reference: briareus-windows. Other clients match this structure, differing only as noted here.
Opened from ⚑ in the sidebar strip (＋ New session, WhatsApp, Mail, 📊, ⚑). ⚑ is shown active and carries the count of held rounds as a badge.

Rounds are grouped by PR (repo · PR #n ↗ opens the PR on GitHub), oldest first. Each round is a raised card. The title opens the conversation, and a finding's title or file:line opens the finding on GitHub.

Fix / Optional / Dismiss is a segmented control: picking the same segment again clears it. Clicking the comment box opens a 'Comment on this finding' dialog, and clicking the note opens a 'Note for the fix session' dialog.

Complete appears only when every finding is marked. Before that the card shows 'N findings still unmarked; Complete appears once every finding has a verdict.' The label is 'Complete · send N to be fixed', or 'Complete · nothing to
fix, approve and close' when nothing is marked fix. A confirm dialog comes first ('Start a paid fix session for N findings?' / 'Complete with nothing to fix?' / 'Take this review off the queue?').

A stale round shows a red line: 'The branch moved after this round was reviewed: some of these may already be fixed…'. A read-only token sees '…This device is read-only: the verdicts are given on the dashboard.' with no controls.
Reply opens a dialog titled 'Reply on this finding’s thread'. Delete asks 'Delete this finding from the review?' with a destructive 'Delete from the review' button.
Polls every 7 s and F5 refreshes. ⧉ (Open in a new window) moves the page into its own window. SSH/Slack approvals are not on this screen: the Windows client does not implement them.
Region names (sidebar, canvas, raise, sunken) are the theme.* roles; widths and margins are layout.* in tokens/. Greys only, on purpose.
